analysis: Examined docs/developer/test.md (head text 475-1331; the only changed hunk is lines 920-926 plus the date stamp) and the production_vectors.json patch (prompt-contract vectors). The doc change is a procedural note: the vectors file is regenerated only in darkbloom-platform at an explicit revision, copied byte-for-byte with the revision and SHA-256 recorded, and must pass scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh. This reinforces the existing trust split and adds no new attack surface. The vector patch adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to the Qwen JSON response_format cases. It changes prompt_token_count, block_boundaries chain_hash values and token_ids, and ends the rendered prompt with an empty think block (248068, 271, 248069, 271) instead of a bare newline. Some vectors keep the same prompt_contract_id (8171fec3..., 507d6d7a..., 4b92f730...) while the rendered tokens and chain hashes change. The cache salt uses prompt-contract ID with the block-hash version (T-041), and chain hashes are derived from tokens. So if the contract ID is meant to version the rendered prompt, old prefix-cache entries (30-minute TTL SSD tier) could be keyed under the same scope with different token streams. This is a correctness/staleness concern, not a cross-account confidentiality issue. Hash-chained tokens plus account/model scoping keep entries from different accounts apart, and I can't confirm from the supplied evidence whether the contract ID is meant to cover this input, so I record it as an unverified contract and make no finding. Patch excerpt is truncated (range_map_complete true but excerpt incomplete), so later hunks were only seen via the changed-range map. Provider/coordinator parity of the regenerated vectors (platform sidecar) is outside the supplied evidence. No authorization, encryption, billing or attestation behavior changed.
